prerequisites: Seeded work lab openlaw-docs-41255c61-work built from 3fa407e3; Jonas Weber signs in to the Portal with a fresh magic link from the lab Mailpit.
Seeded active request types: NDA request (required Counterparty name) and Legal question; seeded home deflection links; seeded live Departments. Fictional PDFs are generated by pdf-r1.mjs.
Nadia Haddad (Legal Team Member) in a separate context declines one Request during its upload and reads the Inbox.
scenarios.expected: One Request has the supplied values and successful attachments and appears for its Requester. Missing required values prevent submission; attachment failure is reported without concealing a successfully created Request.
scenarios.actual: Jonas read Before you submit on the Portal home and opened the NDA request card. Title, Description, Department, Urgency and Counterparty name carried an asterisk; Attachments and Needed by did not. Department started at his own Department (Engineering); Urgency started at Medium with Low, Medium, High, Critical. An empty Submit request answered "Fill Title, Description, and Counterparty name first" with each field marked and sent no POST. Choose files with 21 files listed 20 with "A request carries at most 20 files." and Remove took files off. One file chosen and one dropped onto the form were listed. The completed form (Procurement, High) confirmed "Request R-71 is with Legal", showed "Attaching your files…" while uploads were held, reported no failure, and sent one POST. Open request showed the description, both files with original bytes, Procurement, High and the answer, with no edit control; R-71 appeared once under Your requests (first read was a harness timing fault, rechecked on R-71). Nadia saw R-71 as new in the Inbox with no converted record. Nadia, with no profile Department, saw "Choose a Department" and a refusal naming Department. An aborted upload confirmed R-72 with "This file did not attach. Quote R-72 and send it to Legal another way."; R-72 was saved without the file and the file went on a reply. A decline during upload confirmed R-73 with "Add it to a reply on R-73"; the link opened the Declined Request's composer and the file went on a reply. An unknown form address returned to /portal. An aborted submission showed "The request could not be submitted.", kept the Title, and saved no Request.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the technical reviewer; not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.
